question.text: This Mali emperor, a nephew of Sundiata, caused massive devaluation of gold due to his extremely lavish hajj, during which he supposedly built a mosque every Friday.
question.clue: The architect es-Saheli built the Djinguereber Mosque for this man, who also commissioned Sankore University.

swap.text: The first non-white president of South Africa was this former political prisoner who took office in 1994.
swap.clue: He rose to prominence as the leader of Umkhonto we Sizwe, and he gave the "I am prepared to die" speech during the Rivonia Trial.

question.leadin: Answer the following about British explorers.
question.text: This Welshman charted the Congo River while completing his transcontinental exploration of Africa. Earlier, he is believed to have said, "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?" upon finding the missing explorer.
question.clue: The namesake of this man's boat, the Lady Alice, broke off her engagement to him and married another man while he was on assignment for the New York Herald.

swap.text: The leader of the Boer republic of Transvaal was this awesomely bearded politician who received a congratulatory telegram from German Emperor Wilhelm II for defeating the Jameson Raid without assistance from a great power. He humorously believed the world was flat.
swap.clue: In his youth, he was present at the Sand River Convention that created the nation he later led.

question.leadin: A breakaway state from this country revolted after its Issaq people were the victims of a 1980s genocide.
question.text: Name this country where the 1991 overthrow of the dictator Siad Barre ("see-ahd bar-ay") created a failed state where Al-Shabaab emerged. A US helicopter was shot down in this country in 1993.
question.clue: After the dictator Siad Barre was ousted from power in this nation, warlords began to take control of autonomous regions such as Puntland.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about plane crashes in African history.
swap.text: After Cyprien Ntaryamira and Juvenal Habyarimana were assassinated in a plane crash, this event began when the RTLM radio station issued the command "cut down the tall trees."
swap.answerHtml: Rwandan genocide [or Hutu-Tutsi genocide or Hutu-Tutsi conflict; accept 1994 Rwandan conflict or obvious equivalents; prompt on "Rwandan Civil War" or "Rwandan conflict"]
swap.clue: Romeo Dallaire's Shake Hands With the Devil recounts his attempts to stop RTLM propaganda during this event and the death of president Juvenal Habyarimana.

question.text: This kingdom in modern South Africa lost the Battles of Blood River and Ulundi and was earlier led by Shaka, who adopted the innovative buffalo horn formation in battle and replaced the traditional assegai with the iklwa.
question.clue: This polity was defeated at the Battle of Ulundi but previously had defeated the British at Isandlwana, and it pioneered the use of the "buffalo horn" military formation under its leader Cetshwayo.

swap.leadin: Yusuf is an Arab merchant operating in East Africa during the 15th century.
swap.text: He was probably able to communicate with the locals using this Bantu trade language of East Africa which borrows heavily from Arabic due to merchants like him. It's still spoken in those parts today.
swap.clue: A word in this language named a set of villages established by the Arusha (ah-ROO-shah) Declaration called ujamaa(oo-jah-MAH), as proposed by Julius Nyerere (nuhr-AIR-ay).

question.text: De Gaulle was called out of retirement to lead the Fifth Republic in part to help resolve the war led by the National Liberation Front against French occupation of this area.
question.clue: Ahmed Ben Bella served as the first president of this country after a war that led to many pieds-noirs ("p'yay-NWAR") fleeing this country.

swap.leadin: Because this regime required song lyrics to praise its government, Mulatu Astatke pioneered an instrumental jazz genre.
swap.text: Name this regime headed by Mengistu Haile Mariam. The 1985 Live Aid concert delivered relief to a famine exacerbated by the policies of this Ethiopian military regime.
swap.answerHtml: Derg [or Dergue; prompt on Provisional Military Administrative Council or PMAC]
swap.clue: After taking leadership of this regime, one man declared the Qey Shabbir against enemies like the EPRP.

question.leadin: Answer the following about child soldiers.
question.text: The short film Kony 2012 brought to the public's attention that child soldiers were being used in this Joseph Kony led organization, whose obscure ideology combines ethnic primitivism with Christianity.
question.clue: This militia which seeks to establish a theocracy based on the Ten Commandments and is frequently accused of using child conscripts.

swap.text: Soweto and other apartheid-era atrocities were investigated by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission set up in the 1990s by this first black president of South Africa.
swap.clue: This man succeeded F. W. de Klerk in his highest office after being released from 27 years of imprisonment at Robben Island.

question.leadin: Since eunuchs ("YOO-nucks") were much more valuable than normal slaves, Arab slavers had little problem with the fact that most men whom they castrated in this desert died, since they'd still profit by doing so.
question.text: Name this desert across which many slaves were brought by Arab traders. Those traders also conducted a gold-salt trade through this desert in such towns as Aoudaghost.
question.clue: The Sahel borders this region to the south, separating it from the savanna plains.

swap.leadin: This conflict was sparked by the death of Hamad bin Thuwaini and the HMS Glasgow was sunk during an operation in this war.
swap.text: Name this war that lasted about 45 minutes and is sometimes considered to be the shortest war in history.
swap.clue: The initial cause of the war was the death of Hamad bin Thuwaini, which led to a coup by Khalid bin Bargash, who seized the "House of Wonders" or Beit al-Ajaib - a palace located in modern-day Stone Town.

question.text: This man was prime minister of South Africa during Biko's death. This man, who pushed Ian Smith to cede power in Rhodesia, had previously been Minister of Justice during the Rivonia trial of Nelson Mandela.

swap.leadin: This city's medina quarter contains a bustling central square called the Jemaa el-Fnaa.
swap.text: Name this city which lies south of the Tensift River, the dominant city of central Morocco and the first of Morocco's four Imperial cities.
swap.clue: This city, where the building of the El Badi palace was funded by ransom money demanded from the Portuguese after its rulers' victory at the Battle of Alcacer Quibir [al-KAH-ser KEE-beer].

question.leadin: A revolution against this leader began after his Red Beret special forces attacked clans who attempted to overthrow him in 1978.
question.text: Name this military dictator and Hitler mustache enthusiast who targeted the Isaaq and Majeerteen clans. This leader's single-party Marxist-Leninist state maintained ties with the USSR until a failed 1977 invasion of the Ogaden region.
question.clue: In this man's country, GSG 9 commandos launched Operation Fire Magic to liberate the hijacked Lufthansa Flight 181.

swap.text: Gbeto elephant-hunting bands formed the basis of this group, which expanded to include units named for razors and blunderbusses under King Ghezo. King Agaja's regent Hangbe may have formed this group.
swap.answerHtml: Dahomey Amazons [or Amazons of Dahomey; or Agojie, Mino, or Minon; prompt on ahosi; prompt on Amazons or Dahomey soldiers]
swap.clue: The Dahomey famously used these female soldiers, who were recruited from among the king's wives. After the introduction of the slave trade, they often used Danish guns in battle.

question.leadin: This system, which has been widely adopted in Kenya, builds on SMS technology to allow money transfers.
question.text: Identify this pioneering mobile banking system that takes part of its name from the Swahili word for money.

swap.text: A force of tirailleurs arrived in this town on the White Nile in 1898, sparking a namesake crisis between France and Germany whose resolution helped bring about the Entente Cordiale.
swap.clue: It is probably best known as the location of an 1898 war scare that brought to a head the territorial dispute in Africa between France and Britain, its namesake "incident".
